caption:
The most famous 100-mile trail race started as a horse race. 🐎

The Tevis Cup sends riders 100 miles from Squaw Valley to Auburn, California, inside 24 hours. Gordy Ainsleigh rode it in 1971 and 1972, but in 1973 his horse went lame at mile 30. So in August 1974 he came back without a horse, started ten minutes ahead of the riders and ran the whole trail, reaching Auburn in 23:42, the first to do it on foot in under 24 hours. In 1977 it became an official run: 16 signed up and only one finished inside 24 hours. Today it's the Western States 100, so popular that spots go by lottery. The next draw is December 5.
